summary: Backend lifecycle and auth regression tests passed; frontend auth loads, but registration crashes when the vault mounts.

ui_bugs.issue: React runtime overlay appears after successful registration: destroy is not a function; Add value/dashboard controls become unavailable.

integration_issues.issue: Successful registration reaches the vault briefly, then the component crashes due to effect cleanup handling.

action_items: Change Vault's useEffect(load, []) to an effect callback that invokes load without returning the Axios promise; retest registration and all vault controls.
critical_code_review_comments: load returns client.get(...).then(...); passing it directly as useEffect callback makes React treat the Promise as cleanup, producing destroy is not a function in development/StrictMode.
seed_data_creation: Created disposable TEST_ accounts and items; lifecycle test deletes its item.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend auth, protected items, CRUD, reveal, sharing, recovery, and plaintext exclusion passed. Auth UI and Google link loaded. Mobile registration triggered the React runtime overlay before item CRUD could run.
test_credentials: test_credentials.md was empty; disposable accounts were created for testing.
rca of the issue: In App.js Vault defines load as a promise-returning function and uses useEffect(load,[]). React expects an effect callback to return undefined or a cleanup function, but receives the Axios promise; on unmount/StrictMode cleanup it invokes the promise as destroy. Wrap the call: useEffect(() => { load(); }, []).
